note: Routine mail placed before the target email (one or two per episode). Researcher-authored; not on the drive. Varied on purpose: thanks, FYI, schedule questions, a casework-style referral, an opinion, an invitation, a follow-up. None touches a scenario topic (no 911/CAD, glass or recycling, tax-deeded property, Fischer Creek, CTH E or detours). The bulk agent should make sure ordinary drive files answer them: Ice Center public skate schedule and fees; highway resurfacing (CTH R pulverize/pave in the Town of Gibson is already in the status CSV); plow-damaged mailbox policy ($50 or replacement, in the Oct 5 Kracht email; a Highway policy sheet would help); WHEAP energy assistance through Human Services (also fills Human Services and Health); budget hearing Nov 9 (already in the budget message and newsletter) with public comment rules; snowmobile trail grooming agreements (PPC agenda item 7; a Parks file would help); Public Health flu clinics for children; levy figures (budget message); Veterans Service Office location and appointments; passports (County Clerk); Expo parking lot lighting (Public Works/Expo). Avoid the Kiel Lions date conflicting with the calendar (Nov 19 is open).

emails.name: Brenda Schmitz
emails.body:
Hi, when does public skating start at the Ice Center this year and is it still $5? My granddaughter got skates for her birthday and is dying to try them. Thanks!

Brenda

emails.name: Gerald Pankratz
emails.body:
Mr. Stahlberg,

Just a note to say the county highway guys did a nice job on the resurfacing up our way this summer. Smooth as glass now and they cleaned up after themselves. Pass it along.

Gerald Pankratz

emails.name: Lori Kiel
emails.body:
Last winter the county plow knocked over my mailbox twice and I paid for it myself both times. Does the county pay for that? I want to know before the snow starts this year.

Lori

emails.name: Darlene Wojcik
emails.body:
my mom is 81 and on social security, her heating bill was awful last winter. Is there help with heating bills through the county and who does she call? She doesnt do computers.

thank you Darlene

emails.name: Tom Gloe
emails.body:
When is the public hearing on next year's county budget and can regular people speak at it? I'd like to say something about the county tax rate.

Tom Gloe

emails.name: Rich Ebert
emails.body:
Good morning,

The Kiel Lions Club would like to invite the County Executive to speak at our dinner meeting on Thursday, November 19 at 6:30 p.m. at the Kiel Community Center. About 40 members. 15-20 minutes on county issues would be great, and of course dinner is on us.

Rich Ebert
Program Chair, Kiel Lions Club

emails.name: Kyle Sandoval
emails.body:
Are the county snowmobile trails going to be groomed the same as last year? Heard something about the club agreements being changed. I run the trail map for our club and need to know before we print.

Kyle

emails.name: Susan Ottman
emails.body:
Does the county health department still do flu shots for kids? Our pediatrician is booked until December.

Susan

emails.name: Marvin Lemke
emails.body:
I see in the paper the county levy is going up again. Every year its up. The county needs to learn to live within its means like the rest of us. I'm on a fixed income.

Marvin Lemke

emails.name: Jim Heimerl
emails.body:
My dad was in Korea and just went into assisted living. Someone told me the county has a veterans office that helps with VA benefits. Where is it and do I need an appointment?

Jim

emails.name: Ashley Pagel
emails.body:
I emailed last week about getting a passport for my son and nobody wrote back. Do we do that at the courthouse and do we need an appointment? We travel in January.

Ashley

emails.name: Dean Kraus
emails.body:
Not a complaint really, just FYI. The light pole at the north end of the Expo parking lot has been out for a couple weeks. It gets really dark back there when people are leaving the gun show and the rummage sales. Somebody's going to trip.

Dean Kraus
